sourcedFrom: Staccato C2 Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato (Published August 26, 2024)
cleanIntro: A 2011 strip straight out of Staccato's own C2 instructions: slide stop out, slide forward off the frame with your thumb holding the Recoil Master as it clears, guide rod, reverse plug and spring out of the slide, then the barrel. The compensator gets its own cleaning on this pistol — carbon out, a thin film of CLP in.

steps.title: Muzzle in a safe direction
steps.action: Start with the pistol pointed somewhere safe and keep it that way through the whole strip. Staccato opens the C2 procedure with this before anything else is touched, because the next step works the slide.
steps.quote: Ensure the pistol is pointed in a safe direction.
steps.cite: Staccato C2 Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 1

steps.title: Racked, then chamber and mag well both checked
steps.action: Rack the slide to the rear and look into the chamber and into the mag well — both places, not one. An empty chamber over a loaded magazine is still a loaded pistol the moment the slide goes forward again.
steps.quote: Rack the slide to the rear and visually inspect the chamber and mag well to make sure the pistol is empty.
steps.cite: Staccato C2 Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 2

steps.title: Takedown notch lined up with the slide stop knuckle
steps.action: The slide stop is what holds the top end on the lower, so it comes out first. Draw the slide back until the takedown notch sits over the knuckle of the slide stop and hold it there. If the notch is off the knuckle, the slide stop will not come out cleanly.
steps.quote: Pull the slide back to line up to take down notch on the slide with the slide stop knuckle.
steps.cite: Staccato C2 Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, steps 3–4

steps.title: Slide stop pin pushed through from the opposite side and removed
steps.action: With the notch held on the knuckle, push the slide stop pin from the far side of the pistol with a finger or a small tool, then lift the slide stop out. It should move under light pressure; if it resists, the notch has drifted.
steps.quote: Push on the slide stop pin from the opposite side of your pistol using your finger or a small tool and remove the slide stop.
steps.cite: Staccato C2 Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 5

steps.title: Slide eased forward off the frame — thumb on the Recoil Master
steps.action: Run the slide gently forward off the frame rails. As it clears the frame, put your thumb on the Recoil Master guide rod and hold it — the spring is under load and this is the moment it can get away. Do not let go of it yet.
steps.quote: Gently pull the slide forward and off of the frame.
steps.cite: Staccato C2 Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 6

steps.title: Guide rod, reverse plug and spring out of the slide
steps.action: Keeping the guide rod captured under your thumb, pull the guide rod, the reverse plug and the spring out of the slide. No tool comes into it on Staccato's own C2 procedure — your thumb is the capture.
steps.caution: The recoil spring is compressed until the guide rod is out. Keep your thumb on the rod until the assembly is clear of the slide, and keep it pointed away from your face.
steps.quote: Use your thumb to capture the recoil master guide rod, as you clear the frame.
steps.cite: Staccato C2 Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 7

steps.title: Link forward, barrel out of the muzzle end
steps.action: Flip the link forward along the barrel, then draw the barrel out of the muzzle end of the slide. That completes the strip — frame, slide, recoil assembly and barrel. Staccato notes the procedure is the same on a bull-barrel C2 as on a compensated one, and publishes nothing further than this.
steps.quote: Slide the link forward on the barrel and pull it out from the muzzle end of the slide.
steps.cite: Staccato C2 Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 8

deepAbsentReason: Staccato publishes this page as basic disassembly and reassembly — the article describes itself as covering 'basic disassembly/reassembly of the Staccato C2', and it ends at barrel, slide, frame and the recoil assembly. No extractor, firing pin, sear, mainspring housing or grip-module procedure is published on it, and no exploded view accompanies it. For anything beyond what is written, the page directs owners to contact Staccato Customer Service directly. Nothing deeper was invented from it, and the STI-era book's detail strip was not carried over (see sourceChange).

cleaning.name: RAILS, FRAME & FEED RAMP
tasks: Brush and wipe debris off the slide rails
Brush and wipe the frame surfaces

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Brush the bore from breech to muzzle using the memory flex cable, repeating as needed
Put a small amount of CLP on a bore mop and oil the bore
Wipe the excess oil out of the barrel with a clean patch

cleaning.name: COMPENSATOR
tasks: Remove the carbon buildup inside the compensator with a brush or a scraper
Apply a thin layer of CLP to the inside of the comp

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: A few drops of lubricant on the slide rails
A few drops on the barrel contact points

reassembly: Check the link is flipped forward toward the muzzle, then reinstall the barrel.
Insert the reverse plug, the spring and the guide rod.
Hold the recoil system against the barrel with your thumb.

Line the slide rails up with the frame rails and run the slide on. Staccato's own note: the guide rod flange must be pushed up against the barrel and not kicking out toward the frame, and the barrel must not be rotated, or the top end will not slide fully onto the lower.

Look through the slide stop hole in the frame for the link — the slide stop's pin must pass through the hole in the link or the pistol will not function. If it is not lined up, drop it into place with a small tool.
Insert the slide stop into the frame through the link hole and rest it gently against the frame.
Pull the slide back to line the takedown notch up with the slide stop knuckle, then seat the slide stop fully.
Rack the slide to check for proper function.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty, rack the slide several times and confirm it returns fully into battery, then check the slide stop is fully seated in the frame — a slide stop that will not seat has missed the hole in the barrel link.
